after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Find the solution(s) to the equation $2\operatorname{cos}⁡x+2=0$ for $-\pi <x\le \pi .$
after.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation, isolating $\operatorname{cos}⁡x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{cos}⁡x+2 & =0 \\ 2\operatorname{cos}⁡x & =-2 \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡x & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the solutions to $\operatorname{cos}⁡x=-1$ correspond to the values of $x$ at which $\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ attains its minimum value.

Now, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\operatorname{arccos}⁡(-1)=\pi \end{aligned}
$$

Since $\pi $ lies inside the required domain, our first solution is ${x}_{1}=\pi .$

This solution is a quadrantal angle. To find the remaining solutions, we use our knowledge of the cosine function. We know that the cosine function has its minimum values at

$$
x=\pi +2n\pi .
$$

Since the domain $-\pi <x\le \pi $ is one period, and we have already found one minimum value in this period, we conclude that $x=\pi $ is the only solution.

after.problem: Find the solution(s) to the equation $\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x+3}{2}=1$ for ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘}.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation, isolating $\operatorname{cos}⁡x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x+3}{2} & =1 \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡x+3 & =2 \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡x & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the solutions to $\operatorname{cos}⁡x=1$ correspond to the values of $x$ at which $\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ attains its minimum value.

Now, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\operatorname{arccos}⁡(-1)={180}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

Since ${180}^{∘}$ lies inside the required domain, our first solution is ${x}_{1}={180}^{∘}.$

This solution is a quadrantal angle. To find the remaining solutions, we use our knowledge of the cosine function. We know that the cosine function has its minimum values at

$$
x={180}^{∘}+{360}^{∘}\cdot n.
$$

Since the domain ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘}$ is one period, and we have already found one minimum value in this period, we conclude that $x={180}^{∘}$ is the only solution.
